releases.body: # ARMSX2 2.9.2 What's new: **Report a problem.** Found in the library menu, the side drawer and every game's pause menu. Pick what went wrong, add a few words if you like, and see every file and its size before anything is sent. From a game's pause menu the report can carry a save state and a one-frame graphics dump, so we can see the exact scene. You get a report code to paste into Discord or GitHub. Uploads keep going in the background, wait for Wi-Fi when a report is large, and can be stopped and retried. My reports in Settings > App keeps your codes and how each one went. Reports are kept for 90 days and used only to fix bugs. Memory cards, BIOS files and games are never sent, and your RetroAchievements name, network addresses and file paths are taken out of the logs. If ARMSX2 closes unexpectedly while you're using it, it offers to send a crash report the next time it opens, and the GS dump option can start a report with the dump attached. done by @bmdhacks

releases.body:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-4K-pages.AppImage on most distros, or the 16K one on Asahi Linux and other Apple Silicon kernels (run getconf PAGESIZE if unsure)
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst, a 4K-page build
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst, a 4K-page build (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly

## AMD and Vulkan fixes

This update focuses on AMD shader correctness and Vulkan synchronization. These are targeted fixes, not a guarantee that every AMD game or rendering issue is resolved.

- [#273](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/273) keeps depth-compare images floating-point and makes failed atomic compare-exchange operations feed their returned value into the next retry. On AMD's proprietary Vulkan driver, fragment shuffles use a broadcast fallback. Driver optimization is disabled only for compute shaders `EFF3CCBE1438679D` and `F9EA14A22394F5B1`, which have reported multi-minute compilation stalls.

Vulkan barriers now cover indirect dispatch arguments, make compute writes visible to subsequent graphics work, and replace stale wait-for-idle event reuse with a memory barrier.

- The frame dump can also record every texture a pass or compute dispatch samples (`EDEN_NX2_FRAME_DUMP_SAMPLED=1`), and `EDEN_NX2_REJECT_HASH` switches off specific shaders for A/B tests (#87).

## AMD and Vulkan fixes

This update focuses on AMD shader correctness and Vulkan synchronization. These are targeted fixes, not a guarantee that every AMD game or rendering issue is resolved.

- [#273](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/273) keeps depth-compare images floating-point and makes failed atomic compare-exchange operations feed their returned value into the next retry. On AMD's proprietary Vulkan driver, fragment shuffles use a broadcast fallback. Driver optimization is disabled only for compute shaders `EFF3CCBE1438679D` and `F9EA14A22394F5B1`, which have reported multi-minute compilation stalls.
- [#295](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/295) splits misaligned 64-bit and 128-bit storage-buffer accesses into 32-bit words instead of reading or writing the wrong vector. Vulkan barriers now cover indirect dispatch arguments, make compute writes visible to subsequent graphics work, and replace stale wait-for-idle event reuse with a memory barrier.
